previous_statement: After nodes 1.2, 1.3, 1.4.1, and 1.4.2 are validated, their combination proves this bridge: 1.4.2 supplies the base a_1>=r_+; 1.4.1 supplies r_+/2>1/8>r_- and r_+>=1-C_diag e; and 1.2 plus 1.3 show that a_{2^k}>=r_+ implies a_{2^{k+1}}>=r_+/2>r_- and hence, by the quadratic dichotomy, a_{2^{k+1}}>=r_+. Induction gives the dyadic bounds, and the size monotonicity from 1.3 transfers them to every n.
new_statement: On the nonvanishing-P branch, enlarge the universal square constant to K_sq=max{K_sq^(1),C_ca}, where K_sq^(1) is any constant used for the level-one estimate and C_ca is from lem-compcb-corner-algebra, and include e_ca in the threshold. Since that lemma makes S_P an extended C_ca*e-C*-algebra, its amplified C*-axiom supplies ||Z^dagger dot Z|| >= (1-C_ca*e)||Z||^2 >= (1-K_sq*e)||Z||^2 for every n and Z in M_n tensor S_P. Thus node 1.2's explicit square premise holds at every dyadic level. After nodes 1.2, 1.3, 1.4.1, and 1.4.2 are validated with this enlarged K_sq, node 1.4.2 gives a_1>=r_+, node 1.4.1 gives r_+/2>1/8>r_- and r_+>=1-C_diag*e, and nodes 1.2 and 1.3 give a_{2^(k+1)}>=r_+/2>r_- together with the quadratic dichotomy, hence a_{2^(k+1)}>=r_+. Induction gives all dyadic bounds, and node 1.3's size monotonicity transfers them to every n. The S_P=0 branch is separately vacuous by node 1.5.
